cards.headline: A six-minute overture, released the day it was announced
cards.snippet: On 21 April 2021, Little Simz announced her fourth album and released its opener the same day: a six-minute track produced by Inflo that spends its first minute on marching drums, brass and choir before she raps a word. Stereogum heard it as an overture 'setting the stakes' for the album; the release framing described lives 'lived in the cross-hairs of society, fueled by fear, exhaustion, frustration, but also a kind of white hot political awakening.' It premiered as Annie Mac's Hottest Record on BBC Radio 1.
cards.context: Wikipedia album article and Stereogum's release-day write-up; premiere via Record of the Day.

cards.headline: The album's title is her name, spelled out
cards.snippet: Sometimes I Might Be Introvert is a backronym of Simbi, part of her full first name, Simbiatu. She told The Guardian: 'I'm just very to myself and I didn't know how to really navigate that, especially coming in this industry where you're expected to have this extroverted persona all the time.' The song opens an album about exactly that tension — and the album went on to win the 2022 Mercury Prize.
cards.context: Wikipedia album article — title and concept section, quoting The Guardian.

cards.headline: The line that names her method: anthropologist
cards.snippet: Not literal fieldwork — the annotation reads the line as her method: a fascination with people, and a drive to understand the society around her. The word itself is Greek for 'the study of humanity' — and studying humanity is the song's whole project.
cards.context: Three listeners quote it straight back in the top comments — 'what a line,' says one; 'WHAT A BAR SIS,' says another.

lyric.excerptOrTimestamp: I study humans, that makes me an anthropologist

cards.headline: She sinks into the background of her own video
cards.snippet: I love how she's willing to sink into the background of her own video to offer others space and to help push her narrative as well. An amazing artist.
cards.context: A reading of the video's staging: the star steps back so the dancers and the story carry the frame.

cards.headline: Tiny Desk (Home), 2021: the opener at living-room scale
cards.snippet: NPR's Tiny Desk (home) concert, posted 31 August 2021 — three days before the album — opens with 'Introvert', a full live band re-voicing Inflo's orchestral arrangement in a living room dropped inside a void. One listener: "The backing singers are so well selected for her voice. Really great choices."
cards.context: NPR Music's set list opens with 'Introvert', ahead of 'I Love You, I Hate You', a premiere of 'Point and Kill' with Obongjayar, and 'Woman'.

cards.headline: London, 2022: Introvert & Woman at the BRITs
cards.snippet: At the BRIT Awards on 8 February 2022 she performed 'Introvert' into 'Woman' at London's O2 Arena, with Emma Corrin narrating live and BRIT School dancers around her — the night she won Best New Artist. One listener: "This is Kendrick levels of rap performance, so good"
cards.context: Uploaded to her own channel; produced by BRIT Awards Ltd. Streams of 'Introvert' rose 812% in the performance's wake (Stylist).
